subject: Clarify: patient photo uploads — PHI classification & BAA implications
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@luminahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Mehta <raj.mehta@luminahealth.com>, Lumina Health Legal <legal@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: are patient-submitted photos PHI for our use case?

Hi Evelyn,

Quick question as we prep for production: our patients upload photos (IDs, medication labels, and wound images) as part of intake for one of our digital clinics. We want to confirm whether those images would be considered PHI under typical BAA discussions with a vendor like Redwood.

Context: the images are tied to a patient record (name + DOB) in our system; we currently plan to send images to Redwood's hosted inference API for OCR and metadata extraction (no persistent storage on your side other than short-lived cache for inference).

Primary asks:
- Do you consider personally identifiable images that are linked to patient records PHI?
- If yes, would that make the hosted API ineligible and require Dedicated or Private deployment (or a signed BAA) to process them?
- What evidence or artifacts do you need from us to scope a BAA (dataflow diagram, DPIA, or sample payload)?

Appreciate a brief guidance so our security team can decide next steps.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Integrations, Lumina Health
---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: are patient-submitted photos PHI for our use case?

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear context. Short answer up front: yes — images that are both (a) related to an identified or identifiable patient and (b) used for care/processing are generally treated as PHI for BAA discussions. Whether you need Dedicated/Private or a BAA for hosted depends on how the data is processed, retained, and linked.

Key points to consider (summary):
- PHI classification: any image that can be reasonably associated with a patient (ID card, face, tattoo plus name/DOB metadata, or wound photo when stored against a patient record) should be treated as PHI.
- Hosted API eligibility: Redwood's hosted inference can process PHI for customers under a signed BAA with appropriate contract amendments and controls, but we may require configuration limits (no long-term retention, strict access controls) or recommend Dedicated/Private for high-risk workloads.
- Deployment recommendation: if images are sent with direct patient identifiers and you require guaranteed data isolation, Dedicated or Private deployment reduces surface area. Hosted + BAA is possible for lower-volume or lower-risk flows with strict S3 segregation and short TTLs.

I'll loop in Dev for the technical specifics we would need to scope a BAA and Marissa to kick off the legal template. Attached: a short BAA draft and our SOC2 report reference.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share a dataflow diagram (what you provided as "lumina-image-dataflow-sketch.png" would be perfect).
2) Provide a representative sample payload (redacted) or field list.
3) Confirm retention/TTL expectations and whether you need long-term storage on Redwood.
4) Let us know your risk appetite for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private.

Cc'ing Dev and Marissa.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: soc2-report-2024.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@luminahealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: are patient-submitted photos PHI for our use case?

Hi Aisha — quick technical notes on the image handling side:  

1) Transit and storage: all inbound images to hosted API are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3). For hosted customers we write inference artifacts to short-lived object storage with strict access ACLs; retention is configurable and defaults to 24 hours. If you need zero-persist, we can enable in-memory-only processing for specific routes (with trade-offs in scalability).

2) Metadata linkage: if the request includes explicit PII fields (name, DOB, patient ID), then the image + metadata combination is PHI. If you can pseudonymize or hash identifiers client-side before sending, that can reduce risk but won't eliminate it for BAA scope unless you maintain the mapping outside Redwood.

3) Recommended evidence we need from you to scope BAA:
   - High-level dataflow diagram (redwood uses it to map data at rest/transit).
   - Example JSON payload (redacted) showing the fields you send.
   - Expected throughput/volume (avg images/day, max concurrent).
   - Expected retention TTL and any downstream storage.

4) If you want a conservative path: Dedicated pool with our recommended KV-cache TTL set to 0 and object retention disabled. That would be the simplest from a compliance posture.

I'll review your diagram once you share. Happy to set a tech call if useful.

- Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify: are patient-submitted photos PHI for our use case?

Hi Aisha / Lumina Legal team —

Thanks for the diagram and sample notes. To answer the legal questions succinctly:  

1) Hosted + BAA: Yes, Hosted can be used under a signed BAA with explicit clauses about retention, access controls, and data processing limitations. We'll capture retention TTLs (e.g., 0/24/72 hours) and scope of personnel access in the BAA. For higher-risk flows (IDs and identity documents), we commonly recommend Dedicated/Private but do not mandate it — we evaluate on per-customer risk/volume and contractual controls.

2) Client-side hashing: Hashing patient_id client-side reduces identifiability but does not automatically remove data from BAA scope if the data can be re-associated by you later. The BAA scope is driven by whether Redwood processes data that is reasonably identifiable; pseudonymization can lower risk and may allow more flexible hosting, but legal must accept that control.

3) Audit artifacts: we can include SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, access log exports for the time window you request, and KMS key rotation records (summary). We'll provide templates and examples; production-grade artifacts will require an NDA/addendum in some cases.

Next steps:
- I'll prepare a tailored BAA addendum reflecting retention TTLs and the specific image processing route.
- Dev will work with you to evaluate whether in-memory-only processing on Hosted meets your throughput needs; if not, we'll surface Dedicated pricing and a migration checklist.
- Plan a 30-minute tech/compliance call — suggested times this week: Thu 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 09:00-11:00 PT.

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and attach the BAA draft for your review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
